### Q6. A patient develops fever, chills and flank pain soon after a red cell transfusion starts. What is the immediate action?

Source bank Q3.

- **A.** Administer the next unit
- **B.** Finish the current unit before reporting
- **C.** Stop the transfusion and initiate the reaction protocol with patient assessment
- **D.** Increase the rate

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: C. Stop the transfusion and initiate the reaction protocol with patient assessment**

<!-- job5-rationale -->

Fever, chills aur flank pain acute hemolytic reaction ya bacterial contamination jaisi serious reaction ka warning ho sakte hain. Transfusion immediately stop karo. ABC, vitals aur patient identity assess karo, urgent medical help aur blood bank ko notify karo. Existing blood tubing se flush mat karo. Local protocol ke hisaab se new tubing aur compatible saline se access maintain karo, aur implicated unit preserve karo. Is serious reaction mein transfusion restart mat karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**

- **A (Galat):** Agli unit lagana cause clarify hone se pehle unsafe hai.
- **B (Galat):** Current unit complete hone tak wait karna reaction worsen kar sakta hai.
- **C (Sahi):** Stop karna further exposure rokta hai aur reaction protocol timely activate karta hai.
- **D (Galat):** Rate badhane se suspected harmful exposure aur badh sakta hai.

**Exam clue:** Suspected serious transfusion reaction: stop, assess, escalate.

**Clinical reference:** [Clinical guidance](https://www.lifeblood.com.au/health-professionals/clinical-practice/adverse-events/management-of-suspected-reactions)

**Indian guidance:** [DGHS Blood Transfusion Services and national standards/manual overview](https://www.dghs.mohfw.gov.in/bts.php).

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q32. Before starting a blood transfusion, which verification is essential?

Source bank Q1.

- **A.** Check only the blood bag color
- **B.** Use the room number as identification
- **C.** Assume all units from the blood bank are for this patient
- **D.** Match patient identifiers, compatibility details, component and prescription using approved checks

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: D. Match patient identifiers, compatibility details, component and prescription using approved checks**

<!-- job5-rationale -->

Blood transfusion mein kisi doosre patient ke liye compatible unit galti se lag jaaye toh severe hemolysis, yani red cells ka tootna, ho sakta hai. Bedside par approved independent check ke through patient ke verified identifiers, prescription, component, unit number, compatibility label, expiry aur bag integrity check karo. Mismatch ho toh transfusion start mat karo aur blood bank se clarify karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**

- **A (Galat):** Bag color blood group ya compatibility confirm nahi karta.
- **B (Galat):** Room number patient ka unique identifier nahi hota.
- **C (Galat):** Blood bank delivery alone bedside verification replace nahi karti.
- **D (Sahi):** Patient aur component ka complete match wrong-blood transfusion ka risk kam karta hai.

**Exam clue:** Patient-unit match before transfusion.

**Clinical reference:** [Clinical guidance](https://www.lifeblood.com.au/health-professionals/clinical-practice/transfusion-process/administration-blood-components)

**Indian guidance:** [DGHS Blood Transfusion Services and national standards/manual overview](https://www.dghs.mohfw.gov.in/bts.php).

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q70. After a suspected transfusion reaction, what should happen to the implicated blood bag and tubing?

Source bank Q4.

- **A.** Reuse them for another patient
- **B.** Discard immediately without reporting
- **C.** Hide them until the shift ends
- **D.** Retain and handle them according to the blood bank investigation protocol

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: D. Retain and handle them according to the blood bank investigation protocol**

<!-- job5-rationale -->

Reaction ke baad bag aur administration tubing investigation mein important evidence hote hain. Blood bank unit identity, compatibility aur suspected contamination evaluate kar sakta hai. Bag aur set ko approved biohazard handling ke saath preserve aur return karo. Required fresh patient samples aur incident documentation local protocol ke hisaab se arrange karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**

- **A (Galat):** Reuse se contamination aur wrong-patient exposure ka serious risk hai.
- **B (Galat):** Immediate disposal investigation ke evidence ko destroy kar sakti hai.
- **C (Galat):** Concealment urgent investigation aur patient safety delay karta hai.
- **D (Sahi):** Protocol ke according retained unit aur tubing investigation support karte hain.

**Exam clue:** Preserve implicated component and set.

**Clinical reference:** [Clinical guidance](https://www.lifeblood.com.au/health-professionals/clinical-practice/adverse-events/management-of-suspected-reactions)

**Indian guidance:** [DGHS Blood Transfusion Services and national standards/manual overview](https://www.dghs.mohfw.gov.in/bts.php).

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q72. Which observation provides a baseline for monitoring transfusion reactions?

Source bank Q2.

- **A.** Only a weight from last year
- **B.** Only the bag volume
- **C.** Only the patient's age
- **D.** Vital signs and relevant clinical status before starting

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: D. Vital signs and relevant clinical status before starting**

<!-- job5-rationale -->

Baseline vital signs transfusion se pehle patient ki condition ka starting record hain. Temperature, pulse, BP, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation as indicated aur existing symptoms document karo. Initial period mein closely observe karo aur local policy ke according monitoring repeat karo. New symptoms baseline se compare karne par reaction jaldi identify ho sakti hai.

**Option-wise explanation:**

- **A (Galat):** Purana weight current physiological condition nahi batata.
- **B (Galat):** Bag volume patient ki baseline status nahi batata.
- **C (Galat):** Age risk assessment mein useful ho sakti hai, lekin reaction ke liye baseline vitals nahi hai.
- **D (Sahi):** Baseline vital signs aur clinical status new deterioration identify karne mein help karte hain.

**Exam clue:** Baseline assessment before blood administration.

**Clinical reference:** [Clinical guidance](https://www.lifeblood.com.au/health-professionals/clinical-practice/transfusion-process/administration-blood-components)

**Indian guidance:** [DGHS Blood Transfusion Services and national standards/manual overview](https://www.dghs.mohfw.gov.in/bts.php).

### Q15. A patient develops acute hypoxemia and bilateral lung infiltrates during or within hours of transfusion without clear circulatory overload. Which complication should be considered?

Source bank Q6.

- **A.** Transfusion-related acute lung injury
- **B.** A normal post-transfusion change
- **C.** Simple dehydration
- **D.** Chronic iron overload alone

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: A. Transfusion-related acute lung injury**

<!-- job5-rationale -->

TRALI transfusion-related acute lung injury hai. Lung capillaries leak karne par fluid air sacs mein aa sakta hai, bina primarily cardiac volume overload ke. Acute hypoxemia aur bilateral pulmonary edema during ya within six hours transfusion ke compatible clues hain. Transfusion stop karo, ABC aur oxygenation assess karo aur urgent medical help aur blood bank ko notify karo. TACO, sepsis aur other causes exclude karne ke liye clinical review zaroori hai.

**Option-wise explanation:**

- **A (Sahi):** TRALI is pattern ke liye relevant serious reaction hai. Diagnosis further assessment se hota hai.
- **B (Galat):** New hypoxemia normal transfusion response nahi hai.
- **C (Galat):** Simple dehydration acute bilateral lung edema pattern explain nahi karti.
- **D (Galat):** Chronic iron overload usually repeated transfusions ke baad develop hota hai, immediate lung injury pattern nahi.

**Exam clue:** TRALI: acute hypoxemia and bilateral edema, usually within six hours.

**Clinical reference:** [Clinical guidance](https://www.lifeblood.com.au/health-professionals/clinical-practice/adverse-events/TRALI)

**Indian guidance:** [DGHS Blood Transfusion Services and national standards/manual overview](https://www.dghs.mohfw.gov.in/bts.php).

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q57. Why should a medication not be added directly to a blood component bag?

Source bank Q8.

- **A.** It may be incompatible, contaminate the product or cause a dosing or identification error
- **B.** All drugs are guaranteed compatible with red cells
- **C.** Blood products neutralize every medication
- **D.** Adding medications is required for routine transfusion

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: A. It may be incompatible, contaminate the product or cause a dosing or identification error**

<!-- job5-rationale -->

Blood component ek carefully prepared biological product hai. Direct medicine addition se chemical incompatibility, clotting, contamination aur incorrect dose ka risk ho sakta hai. Medication ke liye separate approved route ya lumen arrange karo aur compatibility pharmacist aur blood bank se verify karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**

- **A (Sahi):** Unapproved medicine addition product safety aur dose accuracy affect kar sakti hai.
- **B (Galat):** Universal drug compatibility established nahi hai.
- **C (Galat):** Blood har drug ko neutralize nahi karta.
- **D (Galat):** Routine transfusion mein medicines bag mein add karna required nahi hai.

**Exam clue:** Never add medication directly to a blood component bag.

**Clinical reference:** [Clinical guidance](https://www.lifeblood.com.au/health-professionals/clinical-practice/transfusion-process/administration-blood-components)

**Indian guidance:** [DGHS Blood Transfusion Services and national standards/manual overview](https://www.dghs.mohfw.gov.in/bts.php).

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q68. During transfusion an older patient develops dyspnea, hypertension and signs of volume overload. Which complication is particularly relevant?

Source bank Q5.

- **A.** An uncomplicated vasovagal reaction
- **B.** Expected therapeutic response
- **C.** Isolated iron deficiency
- **D.** Transfusion-associated circulatory overload

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: D. Transfusion-associated circulatory overload**

<!-- job5-rationale -->

TACO ka full form transfusion-associated circulatory overload hai. Transfused volume patient ke heart aur circulation ki capacity se zyada ho jaaye toh fluid lungs mein jama ho sakta hai. Dyspnea, rising BP, crackles, raised JVP aur positive fluid balance clues ho sakte hain. Transfusion stop karo, ABC assess karo aur urgent help lo. Oxygen, positioning aur prescribed diuretics clinical assessment ke according use hote hain. TACO aur TRALI overlap bhi kar sakte hain.

**Option-wise explanation:**

- **A (Galat):** Vasovagal reaction mein aksar BP fall aur relative bradycardia hoti hai, volume overload typical nahi.
- **B (Galat):** New dyspnea aur hypertension ko expected response nahi maan sakte.
- **C (Galat):** Iron deficiency acute pulmonary fluid overload explain nahi karti.
- **D (Sahi):** TACO mein excess circulatory volume respiratory distress cause kar sakta hai.

**Exam clue:** TACO: respiratory distress with evidence of overload.

**Clinical reference:** [Clinical guidance](https://www.lifeblood.com.au/health-professionals/clinical-practice/adverse-events/TACO)

**Indian guidance:** [DGHS Blood Transfusion Services and national standards/manual overview](https://www.dghs.mohfw.gov.in/bts.php).

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q89. Which IV fluid is conventionally compatible with standard red-cell administration, subject to blood bank policy?

Source bank Q7.

- **A.** 0.9% sodium chloride
- **B.** 5% dextrose as the universal compatible solution
- **C.** Sterile water
- **D.** An arbitrary calcium-containing solution

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: A. 0.9% sodium chloride**

<!-- job5-rationale -->

0.9% sodium chloride isotonic normal saline hai aur standard red-cell administration ke saath universally compatible crystalloid mana jaata hai. Blood administration set, filter aur local blood bank policy follow karo. Other solutions ko same line mein tabhi use karo jab specific compatibility established ho.

**Option-wise explanation:**

- **A (Sahi):** Normal saline standard compatible option hai.
- **B (Galat):** Dextrose-containing fluid red cells ko damage kar sakti hai aur universally compatible nahi hai.
- **C (Galat):** Sterile water alone hypotonic hai aur hemolysis cause kar sakta hai.
- **D (Galat):** Calcium-containing fluids ko routine compatible assume nahi karte. Citrated blood ke saath clotting concern ho sakta hai.

**Exam clue:** Blood line: 0.9% saline, approved set and policy.

**Clinical reference:** [Clinical guidance](https://www.lifeblood.com.au/health-professionals/clinical-practice/transfusion-process/administration-blood-components)

**Indian guidance:** [DGHS Blood Transfusion Services and national standards/manual overview](https://www.dghs.mohfw.gov.in/bts.php).

### Q9. Which blood component primarily increases oxygen-carrying capacity in an anemic patient when transfusion is indicated?

Source bank Q9.

- **A.** Platelet concentrate
- **B.** Cryoprecipitate
- **C.** Packed red blood cells
- **D.** Fresh frozen plasma

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: C. Packed red blood cells**

<!-- job5-rationale -->

Red blood cells mein hemoglobin hota hai jo lungs se oxygen tissues tak carry karta hai. Packed red cells transfusion se circulating red-cell mass aur oxygen-carrying capacity increase ho sakti hai. Transfusion ka decision Hb value alone par nahi, bleeding, symptoms aur clinical context par depend karta hai.

**Option-wise explanation:**

- **A (Galat):** Platelets primary clot formation mein help karte hain, oxygen capacity replace nahi karte.
- **B (Galat):** Cryoprecipitate mainly fibrinogen-rich component hai.
- **C (Sahi):** Packed red cells hemoglobin aur red-cell mass provide karte hain.
- **D (Galat):** Plasma soluble clotting factors provide karti hai, red-cell concentrate nahi.

**Exam clue:** PRBC: oxygen-carrying capacity.

**Clinical reference:** [Clinical guidance](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK594497/)

**Indian guidance:** [DGHS Blood Transfusion Services and national standards/manual overview](https://www.dghs.mohfw.gov.in/bts.php).

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q36. Which blood component contains concentrated fibrinogen and selected clotting proteins?

Source bank Q12.

- **A.** Cryoprecipitate
- **B.** Crystalloid
- **C.** Platelet-poor saline
- **D.** Packed red cells

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: A. Cryoprecipitate**

<!-- job5-rationale -->

Cryoprecipitate plasma ka cold-insoluble fraction hai. Isme concentrated fibrinogen aur factor VIII, XIII, von Willebrand factor jaise selected proteins hote hain. Fibrinogen fibrin clot banane mein important hai. Specific bleeding aur low fibrinogen situation mein authorized replacement plan follow karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**

- **A (Sahi):** Cryoprecipitate fibrinogen-rich blood component hai.
- **B (Galat):** Crystalloid fluid aur electrolytes provide kar sakti hai, coagulation proteins nahi.
- **C (Galat):** Saline clotting proteins supply nahi karti.
- **D (Galat):** Packed red cells mainly hemoglobin supply karte hain.

**Exam clue:** Cryoprecipitate: fibrinogen-rich component.

**Clinical reference:** [Clinical guidance](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK594497/)

**Indian guidance:** [DGHS Blood Transfusion Services and national standards/manual overview](https://www.dghs.mohfw.gov.in/bts.php).

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q50. A patient with a clinically indicated multiple clotting factor deficiency receives plasma. Which purpose is relevant?

Source bank Q11.

- **A.** Replace all electrolytes without volume
- **B.** Provide soluble coagulation factors
- **C.** Provide only concentrated red cells
- **D.** Increase platelet count as the main effect

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: B. Provide soluble coagulation factors**

<!-- job5-rationale -->

Coagulation factors blood proteins hain jo clot ko stable banane ke liye cascade mein kaam karte hain. Plasma multiple soluble factors contain karti hai. Specific bleeding situation aur factor deficiency mein authorized indication ke according plasma use ho sakti hai. Routine volume expansion ya isolated lab abnormality alone automatic indication nahi hai.

**Option-wise explanation:**

- **A (Galat):** Plasma fluid volume bhi deliver karti hai aur all electrolyte replacement ka product nahi hai.
- **B (Sahi):** Soluble coagulation factors replace karna relevant purpose hai.
- **C (Galat):** Red-cell concentrate plasma se alag component hai.
- **D (Galat):** Platelet count badhana plasma ka primary role nahi hai.

**Exam clue:** Plasma: multiple coagulation factors when indicated.

**Clinical reference:** [Clinical guidance](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK594497/)

**Indian guidance:** [DGHS Blood Transfusion Services and national standards/manual overview](https://www.dghs.mohfw.gov.in/bts.php).

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q74. Which blood component is commonly prescribed to replace platelets in clinically indicated thrombocytopenia?

Source bank Q10.

- **A.** Normal saline
- **B.** Packed red cells
- **C.** Albumin alone
- **D.** Platelet concentrate

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: D. Platelet concentrate**

<!-- job5-rationale -->

Platelets chhote cell fragments hain jo injured blood vessel par primary plug banane mein help karte hain. Clinically indicated thrombocytopenia, yani low platelet count, ya selected platelet dysfunction mein platelet concentrate prescribe ho sakta hai. Bleeding risk aur condition-specific thresholds consider hote hain.

**Option-wise explanation:**

- **A (Galat):** Normal saline fluid volume provide karti hai, platelets nahi.
- **B (Galat):** Packed red cells platelet replacement ka standard component nahi.
- **C (Galat):** Albumin plasma protein solution hai, platelets provide nahi karti.
- **D (Sahi):** Platelet concentrate indicated platelet replacement ke liye appropriate hai.

**Exam clue:** Platelets: primary hemostasis.

**Clinical reference:** [Clinical guidance](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK594497/)

**Indian guidance:** [DGHS Blood Transfusion Services and national standards/manual overview](https://www.dghs.mohfw.gov.in/bts.php).

### Q11. A patient with cardiac disease receives IV fluid and develops new crackles and increasing work of breathing. What should the nurse do?

Source bank Q16.

- **A.** Increase fluid rate
- **B.** Assess respiratory and circulatory status and urgently review the infusion plan
- **C.** Encourage a large oral fluid bolus
- **D.** Wait for the bag to empty

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: B. Assess respiratory and circulatory status and urgently review the infusion plan**

<!-- job5-rationale -->

Cardiac disease mein heart extra IV fluid efficiently handle nahi kar paata toh pulmonary congestion develop ho sakti hai. New crackles aur increased breathing effort urgent deterioration ke clues hain. ABC, oxygen saturation, vital signs aur infusion assess karo. Suspected harmful infusion ko local emergency protocol ke mutabik pause karo aur urgent medical review lo. Prescribed treatment plan follow karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**

- **A (Galat):** Rate increase overload aur breathing difficulty worsen kar sakta hai.
- **B (Sahi):** Immediate assessment aur urgent infusion-plan review safest action hai.
- **C (Galat):** Large oral bolus fluid load worsen kar sakta hai.
- **D (Galat):** Bag empty hone tak wait respiratory compromise worsen kar sakta hai.

**Exam clue:** New crackles during IV therapy: urgent assessment.

**Clinical reference:** [Clinical guidance](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/cg174/chapter/Recommendations)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q48. A patient weighs 62 kg yesterday and 64 kg today using the same scale and comparable conditions. What should the nurse consider?

Source bank Q13.

- **A.** It proves dehydration
- **B.** It proves 2 kg of new muscle was formed overnight
- **C.** The change should never be assessed
- **D.** A 2-kg rapid gain may reflect approximately 2 L of fluid accumulation

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: D. A 2-kg rapid gain may reflect approximately 2 L of fluid accumulation**

<!-- job5-rationale -->

Same scale aur comparable conditions mein weight 64 minus 62 = 2 kg badha hai. Water ki density ke hisaab se 1 kg roughly 1 L ke barabar hota hai. Isliye rapid 2 kg gain approximately 2 L retained fluid ka clue ho sakta hai, exact proof nahi. Edema, breathing, intake-output aur measurement accuracy check karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**

- **A (Galat):** Weight gain dehydration prove nahi karta.
- **B (Galat):** Overnight 2 kg new muscle formation unlikely hai.
- **C (Galat):** Rapid weight change ko ignore karne se overload miss ho sakta hai.
- **D (Sahi):** 2 kg gain roughly 2 L fluid accumulation suggest kar sakta hai.

**Exam clue:** Rapid weight change: about 1 kg per litre of water.

**Clinical reference:** [Clinical guidance](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/cg174/chapter/Recommendations)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q65. Which finding is consistent with possible extracellular fluid volume depletion?

Source bank Q15.

- **A.** Orthostatic dizziness with dry mucosa and reduced urine output
- **B.** Bounding pulse with no other assessment
- **C.** New generalized edema as the only sign
- **D.** Progressive weight gain with crackles

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: A. Orthostatic dizziness with dry mucosa and reduced urine output**

<!-- job5-rationale -->

Extracellular fluid depletion mein blood circulation aur tissue spaces ka fluid kam ho sakta hai. Orthostatic dizziness standing par perfusion change ka clue hai, dry mucosa aur reduced urine output bhi suggestive hain. BP, pulse, perfusion, intake-output, losses aur labs assess karo. Ek isolated sign diagnosis prove nahi karta.

**Option-wise explanation:**

- **A (Sahi):** Orthostatic symptoms, dry mucosa aur low urine output together possible depletion suggest karte hain.
- **B (Galat):** Bounding pulse alone depletion establish nahi karta.
- **C (Galat):** Generalized edema alone typical depletion sign nahi hai, although edema aur intravascular depletion coexist kar sakte hain.
- **D (Galat):** Weight gain aur crackles fluid excess suggest kar sakte hain.

**Exam clue:** Assess multiple volume status clues.

**Clinical reference:** [Clinical guidance](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/cg174/chapter/Recommendations)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q82. A patient's output includes 900 mL urine and 300 mL drain fluid while measured intake is 1500 mL. What is recorded net balance?

Source bank Q14.

- **A.** +300 mL
- **B.** −300 mL
- **C.** +600 mL
- **D.** 2700 mL

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: A. +300 mL**

<!-- job5-rationale -->

Recorded fluid balance mein same observation period ka measured intake minus measured output karte hain. Output = 900 + 300 = 1200 mL. Net = 1500 − 1200 = +300 mL. Positive sign ka matlab recorded intake measured output se zyada hai. Insensible losses aur unrecorded fluids ki wajah se actual body balance different ho sakta hai.

**Option-wise explanation:**

- **A (Sahi):** 1500 − 1200 = +300 mL correct hai.
- **B (Galat):** −300 reverse subtraction se aata hai.
- **C (Galat):** +600 drain output ko omit karta hai.
- **D (Galat):** 2700 intake aur output ka sum hai, net balance nahi.

**Exam clue:** Intake minus all measured output.

**Clinical reference:** [Clinical guidance](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/cg174/chapter/Recommendations)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q7. Which solution is an isotonic crystalloid in common clinical use?

Source bank Q17.

- **A.** 0.45% sodium chloride
- **B.** 3% sodium chloride
- **C.** Sterile water for IV infusion alone
- **D.** 0.9% sodium chloride

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: D. 0.9% sodium chloride**

<!-- job5-rationale -->

Isotonic crystalloid ka effective tonicity plasma ke approximately similar hota hai. 0.9% sodium chloride commonly used isotonic crystalloid hai aur extracellular volume expand kar sakti hai. Fluid indication, sodium, chloride, renal aur cardiac status monitor karo. Large saline volumes hyperchloremia aur acidosis contribute kar sakti hain.

**Option-wise explanation:**

- **A (Galat):** 0.45% saline hypotonic hai.
- **B (Galat):** 3% saline hypertonic hai.
- **C (Galat):** Sterile water alone IV infusion se hemolysis ka risk hai.
- **D (Sahi):** 0.9% saline conventional isotonic crystalloid hai.

**Exam clue:** 0.9% saline isotonic, 0.45% hypotonic, 3% hypertonic.

**Clinical reference:** [Clinical guidance](https://ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK500033/?report=printable)

### Q80. Why should measurable liquid medication and tube flushes be included in intake records?

Source bank Q20.

- **A.** They are always negligible
- **B.** Only drinking water counts as intake
- **C.** They cannot enter the body's water compartments
- **D.** They contribute to administered fluid volume

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: D. They contribute to administered fluid volume**

<!-- job5-rationale -->

Fluid balance sirf drinking water ka record nahi hai. Liquid medicine, enteral feeds, tube flushes aur IV fluids patient ko measurable volume deliver karte hain. Same period mein inhe appropriate intake categories mein record karo. Strict fluid restriction mein small repeated volumes bhi important hote hain.

**Option-wise explanation:**

- **A (Galat):** Small volumes add up ho sakte hain, especially repeated doses mein.
- **B (Galat):** Water alone total intake represent nahi karta.
- **C (Galat):** Liquid medicines aur flushes body fluid balance contribute kar sakte hain.
- **D (Sahi):** Administered liquid volumes ko count karna recorded balance accurate banata hai.

**Exam clue:** Count all measurable administered fluid.

**Clinical reference:** [Clinical guidance](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/cg174/chapter/Recommendations)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q84. Why must hypertonic saline administration be closely monitored?

Source bank Q18.

- **A.** It is physiologically identical to free water
- **B.** It is safe at any rate for every patient
- **C.** It can alter sodium and water distribution rapidly, with serious complications if mismanaged
- **D.** It has no effect on serum sodium

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: C. It can alter sodium and water distribution rapidly, with serious complications if mismanaged**

<!-- job5-rationale -->

Hypertonic saline plasma ke comparison mein higher effective solute concentration rakhti hai. Isse water cells se extracellular space ki taraf shift ho sakta hai aur serum sodium rise kar sakta hai. Severe symptomatic hyponatremia jaise selected indications mein prescribed protocol use hota hai. Rapid inappropriate correction osmotic demyelination aur fluid overload jaise harms cause kar sakti hai. Repeat sodium, neurological status aur fluid status monitor karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**

- **A (Galat):** Free water ka tonicity effect different hota hai.
- **B (Galat):** Any rate par universal safety nahi hai.
- **C (Sahi):** Sodium aur water distribution rapidly change ho sakte hain, isliye close monitoring zaroori hai.
- **D (Galat):** Hypertonic saline serum sodium change kar sakti hai.

**Exam clue:** Hypertonic saline requires protocol and repeat sodium monitoring.

**Clinical reference:** [Clinical guidance](https://ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK500033/?report=printable)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q116. A patient receiving a potassium-containing IV solution has an unexpectedly high potassium result. Which action is safest?

Source bank Q19.

- **A.** Increase potassium delivery
- **B.** Give a rapid unprescribed potassium bolus
- **C.** Assess the patient, verify the result and infusion, and urgently follow the escalation protocol
- **D.** Continue unchanged regardless of the result

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: C. Assess the patient, verify the result and infusion, and urgently follow the escalation protocol**

<!-- job5-rationale -->

Hyperkalemia yani blood potassium zyada hona heart ke electrical conduction ko affect kar sakta hai. Unexpected high result mein patient ko assess karo, ECG aur urgent clinical review arrange karo, sample hemolysis aur infusion contents verify karo. Potassium-containing infusion ko local urgent safety protocol ke mutabik withhold ya pause karo jab tak responsible team review kare. Severe clinical concern mein repeat sample ke liye emergency care delay mat karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**

- **A (Galat):** Extra potassium delivery arrhythmia ka risk badhati hai.
- **B (Galat):** Rapid unprescribed IV potassium bolus life-threatening arrhythmia cause kar sakta hai.
- **C (Sahi):** Assessment, infusion safety check aur escalation potentially dangerous potassium elevation address karte hain.
- **D (Galat):** Unchanged infusion se potassium aur badh sakta hai.

**Exam clue:** High potassium: urgent assessment, stop additional potassium exposure per protocol.

**Clinical reference:** [Clinical guidance](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/cg174/chapter/Recommendations)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>
